stem: The daily wages (in Rs) of seven workers are: 320, 450, 280, 510, 390, 620, 410. What is the range of this data set?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Student uses second-largest minus smallest: 510 - 280 = 230, or confuses which value is the maximum, arriving at 290 by using 570 - 280.
Student computes 620 - 300 = 320, using 300 instead of 280 as the minimum.

explanation: Range is the simplest measure of dispersion. Identify the maximum (620) and minimum (280) values, then subtract: 620 - 280 = 340.

explanation_sections.punchline: Range = Max - Min; scan all values to correctly identify both extremes before subtracting.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the distribution measure needed (range). Scan the data: min = 280, max = 620. Apply Range = Max - Min = 620 - 280 = 340.
explanation_sections.lesson: Range uses only the two extreme values; never use second-largest or a misread extreme.
explanation_sections.timing: 20 seconds. Scan list once for min and max, then subtract. The trap is misreading 280 as 290 or 300.
